tool.name: Mitochondrial DNA variants
tool.description: homoplasmic and heteroplasmic mtDNA variants and the mtDNA haplogroup from the off-target reads of an exome
tool.command: ln -s '$bam' input.bam && ln -s '${bam.metadata.bam_index}' input.bam.bai && ln -s '$reference' reference.fa && samtools faidx reference.fa && python3 '$__tool_directory__/wes_mito.py' --bam input.bam --reference reference.fa #if $gnomad_mt: --gnomad-mt '$gnomad_mt' #end if #if $clinvar: --clinvar '$clinvar' #end if --min-hl $min_hl --min-alt $min_alt --min-depth $min_depth --min-depth-hom $min_depth_hom #if $haplogroup: --haplogroup --sample '$bam.element_identifier' #end if --tsv '$calls' --json '$summary'

param.name: bam
param.label: Aligned reads (BAM)
param.help: Duplicate-marked reads of the sample, aligned to a reference with the mitochondrial genome (MT or chrM, rCRS).

param.name: gnomad_mt
param.label: gnomAD v3.1 chrM sites (VCF)
param.help: gnomad.genomes.v3.1.sites.chrM.vcf.bgz (CC0): homoplasmic/heteroplasmic frequencies, haplogroup-defining flag, MitoTIP and PON-mt-tRNA.

param.name: clinvar
param.label: ClinVar (VCF)
param.help: The ClinVar VCF of the workflow (its MT records are used).

param.name: min_alt
param.label: Reads needed for a heteroplasmic call

param.name: min_depth
param.label: Depth needed for a heteroplasmic call

param.name: min_depth_hom
param.label: Depth needed for a homoplasmic call (at least 90 % of reads)
param.help: Also the depth at which a position counts as covered for the haplogroup.

param.name: haplogroup
param.label: Classify the mtDNA haplogroup (HaploGrep3, PhyloTree 17 Forensic Update 1.2)

tool.help:
**What it does**
Calls mitochondrial DNA variants from the reads of an exome (or genome). Exome captures pull in many mtDNA reads off target: in the GIAB IDT exomes the median depth on chrM was 11-14x in one library batch and 39-121x in the other. The reads are piled up with samtools (MAPQ >= 20, which removes most reads of nuclear mitochondrial segments, base quality >= 20). An allele is called **homoplasmic** when it is in >= 90 % of >= 5 reads and **heteroplasmic** when it is in >= 10 % of >= 20 reads with >= 3 supporting reads (all adjustable).
Each call is annotated with ClinVar, the gnomAD v3.1 mitochondrial frequencies (homoplasmic and heteroplasmic among 56,434 genomes, highest heteroplasmy seen, haplogroup-defining flag), MitoTIP and PON-mt-tRNA predictions for tRNA variants, and the rCRS gene. Flags: one strand only, the artefact-prone homopolymers (302-316, 513-525, 16182-16194), and heteroplasmy below 50 %.
**Mixture check.** A second mtDNA lineage, from contamination or from nuclear mitochondrial segments captured with the exome, shows as heteroplasmy at positions that are common homoplasmic variants of other haplogroups (gnomAD >= 1 %). Three or more such sites are reported in the summary; low heteroplasmy is then unreliable in that sample.
**Haplogroup.** The majority allele of every position covered by at least 5 reads is classified with HaploGrep3 against PhyloTree 17 Forensic Update 1.2. Exomes cover the mtDNA unevenly, so HaploGrep3 is given the covered ranges (HSD format): an uncovered position is unknown, not the rCRS base. HaploGrep3's quality counts the covered positions only, so the confidence also needs coverage: **high** = at least 40 % of the mtDNA covered and quality >= 0.9, **medium** = quality 0.8-0.9, **low** otherwise. In 104 1000 Genomes exomes (tests/haplogroup_eval.py) no high- or medium-confidence call was on a wrong branch; the wrong calls were all below 26 % coverage. The summary lists the best three haplogroups, the expected variants not found and the extra (private) variants.
**Outputs**: a table of calls and a JSON summary (coverage, the heteroplasmy detectable at the median depth, counts, the mixture check, the depth at the CPIC MT-RNR1 positions 1095, 1494 and 1555, and the haplogroup). The clinical report shows them in its mitochondrial section.
